Let me know, if I should run any specific tests @hawkinsp .
I've asked some folks from NVIDIA to take a look (might be next week).

Are there any updates on this by any chance?

In the mean time, I was able to reproduce the issue on a 6 x RTX 6000 Ada Generation machine.

So it seems that the issue primarly affects newer generation NVIDIA GPUs.

Unfortunately I wasn't able to reproduce your failure using a recent nightly container `ghcr.io/nvidia/jax:jax-2025-09-15` on a machine with 8xL40S, although the machine I found does not report exactly the same topology. I'll see if I can find one that matches more closely. I've asked internally for other pointers.

(Your machine does not have NVLink connections between the GPUs, so setting `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL` should just be disabling the P2P path and forcing communication via (host) shared memory. That is shown in the logs you attached. Attaching a debug log without setting `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL` would show what default it is choosing for your machine's topology).

Thank you for your prompt answer @olupton !
I attach two logs with `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL` unset.
One is from a 8xL40s machine and the other from a 6xRTX6000 Ada machine.
The former belongs to my university (nvidia-smi topo already sent in previous message) which I have more access to for testing, the latter is from a paid runpod.io instance (plain ubuntu template) if you want to test it there as well.

[rtx6000_test.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22408740/rtx6000_test.txt)
[l40s_test.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22408867/l40s_test.txt)

I'm going to focus on the `all_reduce_perf` run _without_ `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL` which, as you said, hangs. If something so fundamental doesn't work, then there's a serious issue on the node that must be resolved before it makes any sense to look at application output.

Please consult the [Troubleshooting](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/user-guide/docs/troubleshooting.html) section of the NCCL guide, especially the part about GPU Direct. My first suspicion would be misconfigured ACS preventing CUDA P2P from functioning correctly. That section also has links to p2pBandwidthLatencyTest from cuda-samples and to nvbandwidth, which I would recommend running to verify if the issue is visible only with NCCL or if any application that uses CUDA P2P is affected (I would suspect the latter). You could also try runs on subsets of GPUs by setting `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to values such as `0,1`, `2,3`, `4,5` and `6,7`, to see if you see the problem with any pair of GPUs or with only one of them.

Thanks for your pointers @kiskra-nvidia !
I will try troubleshooting NCCL in the next couple of days.

I'll briefly summarise my observations so far:
- I observed the erroneous output of the test script, e.g.
```
local: [1024. 1024.    0. 1024. 1024.    0. 1024. 1024.]
global_sum: [6144. 6144. 6144. 6144. 6144. 6144. 6144. 6144.]
```
on multiple machines (university and runpod.io nodes) and L40s and RTX6000 Ada GPUs (not ruling out that all of them may be misconfigured).
- I haven't observed this issue on 8 x A40 and 8 x A100
- I run the script with uv: `uv -p python3.13 --with="jax[cuda]" test.py` (I have not tested with the nightly docker containers yet. I think I won't be able to do this on the nodes available to me)
- Sometimes (not always) the `test.py` script just hangs. In this case, setting `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL` at least resolves the hang.
- I have sent logs of a `test.py` run without `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL` set where it does not hang, but produces erroneous output.
- I am able to run many of my pmap JAX programs on 8 x L40s successfully. Even the `test.py` often produces the correct result.
- I have not sufficiently tested with `nccl-test` yet, which I am going to do next.

I run the p2pBandwidthLatencyTest test and attach the result.
`P2P=Enabled Latency (P2P Writes) Matrix (us)` seems high, but I don't have a reference for that.
I am not sure if ACS is misconfigured, `lspci -vvv | grep ACSCtl ` shows nothing.

Currently, the cluster I have access to is very busy and I have not been able to test as much with 8 GPUs.
Furthermore, I encounter the issue less often.
It is a SLURM cluster, so maybe issues stem from oversubscribing resources, I am not sure.
I moved and completed my MCMC experiments on other GPUs, so now I have less spare time to continue testing on L40s.

Thanks again for all the input!

[nccl_troubleshoot_p2p_bandwidth.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22633371/nccl_troubleshoot_p2p_bandwidth.txt)

Yeah, those `P2P=Enabled Latency (P2P Writes) Matrix` numbers, in 50,000us range, are absolutely crazy and indicative of a problem. Coincidentally, just recently I've seen numbers very much like that on one cluster, and it turned out that it was missing the `iommu.passthrough=1` parameter on the Linux kernel commandline. Might be worth a try in your case as well...
Closing because I'm not sure there's much we can do here. Our hypothesis was and remains that it is an issue with the hardware.

issue.body:
### Description

Hello, I have encountered a weird bug where my MCMC program does not work properly  when using 8 L40s GPUs and produces acceptance rates like `-110768.6562` or `21235.4844` where they should be between 0 and 1.  
There seems to be something wrong with pmap (or device communication) and I reduced the bug to the following snippet:

```python
import jax, jax.numpy as jnp

def test_psum(x):
    local = jnp.sum(x) 
    global_sum = jax.lax.psum(local, 'i')
    return local, global_sum

x = jnp.ones((jax.local_device_count(), 1024))
local, global_sum = jax.pmap(test_psum,axis_name="i")(x)
print("local:", local) 
print("global_sum:", global_sum) 
```

Expected result is:
```
local: [1024. 1024. 1024. 1024. 1024. 1024. 1024. 1024.]
global_sum: [8192. 8192. 8192. 8192. 8192. 8192. 8192. 8192.]
```

Observed output is:
```
local: [1024. 1024. 1024. 1024. 1024. 1024.    0. 1024.]
global_sum: [7168. 7168. 7168. 7168. 7168. 7168. 7168. 7168.]
```
```
local: [1024. 1024.    0. 1024. 1024.    0. 1024. 1024.]
global_sum: [6144. 6144. 6144. 6144. 6144. 6144. 6144. 6144.]
```
```
local: [1024.    0.    0.    0.    0.    0.    0.    0.]
global_sum: [1024. 1024. 1024. 1024. 1024. 1024. 1024. 1024.]
```
etc.

Sometimes I get wrong results, sometimes I get the correct result, as I am writing, the script just hangs and does not complete anymore. (The script seems to hang if I don' set `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL`, maybe NVLink causes problems?).

I mostly get this bug on 8 x L40s.  
It works more often on 2 x L40s, and 4 x L40s.  
On 1 x L40s everything is okay.
The bug does not happen on 8 x A40 and 8 x A100s.  
I confirmed this bug on 2 different clusters with 8 x L40s with cuda version 12.8 and 12.9 (posted below).


I attach NCCl logs of a correct and faulty run (setting `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL`).
Please let me know what other information I could provide.
